findings.title: Import-level closures select 9 scripts (525.7 s recorded) for a payload.py function-body edit none of them executes
findings.claim: Of the 170 (script, D3-s2 cell) closure pairs whose traced unmutated run is clean, 29 claim a cell whose function bodies the script never executes and never reads as text, so closure.py select runs that script for any function-body-only edit of that cell although the edit cannot change its run; payload.py alone carries 525.7 s of 3051.3 s recorded selected seconds this way (boost_drift_replay.py 341.1 s, optimality.py 142.5 s, validate.py 21.5 s, guard_pins.py 8.2 s, manual_plan.py 6.5 s, ...).
findings.mechanism: tests/closures.json records the files a run imported or opened (derive_closures.sh); a module imported for its constants or a type is a closure member even when no function of it runs. tests/mutation_table.py already exploits the finer fact (reach_skip / never_reaches) for mutants, but the scoped gate's selection does not.

evidence.unit: over-approximated (script, cell) pairs of 170 clean pairs

perturbation.change: --claim-only tests/boost_drift_replay.py:payload.py (drop that pair from the closure the count reads, the effect of a body-granular closure for that pair)

findings.metric_definition: pairs (script, cell) in closures.json with a clean traced baseline that executed zero function-body lines of the cell and did not read it as text
findings.phenomenon_property: A scoped-gate selection should not run a script for an edit confined to function bodies that script's measured run never executes.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Measure only; a body-granular selection is a gate-design change (module-level edits must still select every importer). At most a closure.py selection refinement that skips a script for a function-body-only hunk in a file its recorded reach never executes, reusing mutation_table.never_reaches.
reproduction_steps: Run prescreen.py to produce run/reach/*.json (traced baselines)

findings.title: No check feeds NaN to score_lead_predictions; dropping its guard poisons lead sigma permanently
findings.claim: Disabling accuracy.py:261 (`if not np.isfinite(actual_temp): return` -> `if False:`) survives all 20 drivers of accuracy.py's measured closure (12 run, 8 reach-skipped; env_drift.py --all against the baseline included), yet on one NaN reading it turns AccuracyTracker.sigma(3.0) from 0.5 to nan and keeps it nan after a later finite scoring.
findings.mechanism: lead_sigma is an EWMA: (1-a)*prev + a*err, so one NaN err makes every later value NaN; the guard is the only barrier inside the tracker, and no test drives a non-finite actual_temp into it.

evidence.contention_note: deterministic; survivor verdict from drive_resumable.py (tally.py: accuracy.py:261 GUARD_OFF LIVES), box shared with D0-s2 and D9-s2 at load ~7

null_control.note: null mutant: baseline and mutant sigma both 0.5; the sibling guard accuracy.py:238 (non-finite predicted) reads 0 too: it is shadowed by the loop's own isfinite(predicted) filter, an equivalent survivor

findings.metric_definition: 1 when AccuracyTracker.sigma(3.0) after a NaN then a finite scoring differs between the baseline module and the in-memory mutant, else 0
findings.phenomenon_property: Every non-finite guard at a learner's state boundary in the cells has a check that feeds it a non-finite value and asserts the learned state stays finite.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Test only: one check (features.py or a unit block) scoring a NaN actual_temp after a finite one and asserting sigma stays finite and lead_counts unchanged; then pin the site killed_by.
